metadata.safety_note: Events are intentionally abstract and contain no exploit steps, targeting guidance, weapons design, hazardous procedures, or safeguard evasion.

scenarios.title: Supplier capacity failure
scenarios.brief: A fictional upstream service reports a sustained capacity problem. Essential workflows remain available, but continuity margins are narrowing.
facts: The dependency is mapped to two essential workflows.
No evidence indicates malicious activity; this is modeled as a service resilience event.
assumptions: The supplier can provide status updates but cannot promise a restoration time.
Alternative capacity exists but has not been exercised at full scope.

choices.label: Activate continuity redundancy
choices.description: Shift to the documented alternate service path and record observed gaps.
choices.why: Exercising an alternate path reduces dependency concentration in the simulation and produces current evidence, while consuming operational capacity.

choices.label: Perform focused supplier review
choices.description: Request continuity evidence, dependency assumptions, and a remediation commitment from the fictional supplier.
choices.why: A focused review improves the basis for risk decisions and supplier governance, but it does not immediately remove the dependency.

choices.label: Increase monitoring and escalation readiness
choices.description: Increase status review cadence and pre-authorize continuity escalation thresholds.
choices.why: Better visibility can shorten decision latency and reduce uncertainty, but monitoring alone does not create alternate capacity.

choices.label: Temporarily accept the exposure
choices.description: Preserve budget and document a time-bounded acceptance with explicit ownership.
choices.why: Capacity is preserved, but the unresolved dependency remains exposed and governance confidence declines without additional mitigation.

scenarios.title: Cryptographic migration horizon
scenarios.brief: A governance review concludes that some long-lived fictional records will remain sensitive beyond the intended assurance lifetime of current cryptographic choices.
facts: The archive contains very long-lived records.
A cryptographic inventory exists and identifies migration candidates.
assumptions: Migration can be staged without changing the underlying business purpose of the records.
No claim is made about a specific future cryptanalytic capability or date.

choices.label: Prioritize cryptographic migration
choices.description: Fund the staged migration backlog for the longest-lived data and highest-criticality services.
choices.why: A staged migration directly improves crypto-agility and reduces the simulated exposure of long-lived information, with a real capacity tradeoff.

choices.label: Deepen inventory and data-longevity review
choices.description: Improve classification, ownership, and migration sequencing before broader change.
choices.why: Better inventory evidence improves confidence and sequencing, but the technical exposure changes only when migration work is executed.

choices.label: Run independent migration assurance
choices.description: Review migration criteria, rollback governance, evidence, and ownership before scaling the program.
choices.why: Independent assurance raises confidence that the migration program is governed correctly without claiming that assurance itself removes obsolescence risk.

scenarios.title: Audit evidence finding
scenarios.brief: An internal audit identifies inconsistent evidence freshness across several fictional controls. The controls may still operate, but the assurance trail is incomplete.
facts: The finding concerns evidence quality and governance consistency.
No operational compromise is asserted by the audit finding.
assumptions: Control owners can produce supplemental evidence within the current planning cycle.
The audit function remains independent from remediation owners.

choices.label: Open owned remediation actions
choices.description: Assign accountable owners, evidence requirements, and closure criteria to the finding.
choices.why: Owned remediation improves auditability and reduces repeat-finding likelihood while consuming near-term capacity.

choices.label: Expand assurance sampling
choices.description: Test a wider sample to determine whether the evidence gap is isolated or systemic.
choices.why: A larger sample improves the basis for the assessment, but it primarily changes confidence rather than the underlying control state.

choices.label: Refresh control-owner training
choices.description: Reinforce evidence expectations, ownership, and review cadence across control operators.
choices.why: Training addresses process consistency and accountability, though additional evidence is still needed to close the finding.

choices.label: Defer remediation to preserve capacity
choices.description: Record the finding and postpone corrective work to a later planning cycle.
choices.why: Deferral preserves capacity but weakens the evidence trail and increases the chance that the governance gap persists.

scenarios.title: Coordination communications outage
scenarios.brief: The fictional coordination network is intermittently unavailable. Core records remain accessible, but teams are relying on slower continuity channels.
facts: The outage affects coordination rather than record integrity.
A documented alternate communications path exists.
assumptions: The alternate path has enough capacity for priority messages.
The primary provider is investigating the service issue.

choices.label: Activate alternate communications
choices.description: Move priority coordination to the documented continuity channel and log exceptions.
choices.why: Using the alternate path demonstrates continuity capability and reduces exposure to the current outage, with some capacity cost.

choices.label: Tighten outage monitoring
choices.description: Track service status, queue health, and escalation checkpoints at a higher cadence.
choices.why: Better observations improve confidence and escalation timing but do not create additional communications capacity.

choices.label: Start supplier continuity review
choices.description: Review outage handling, alternate routing commitments, and service dependency assumptions.
choices.why: Supplier review improves future resilience governance and evidence while the immediate outage remains an operational concern.

scenarios.title: Insider policy exception
scenarios.brief: A fictional staff member used an approved account outside the intended workflow, creating a policy exception that requires governance review.
facts: The event is a policy and accountability issue; no attack method is modeled.
Relevant access records and approvals are available for review.
assumptions: The deviation may reflect process pressure, misunderstanding, or an authorization design gap.
The organization can investigate without presuming malicious intent.

choices.label: Tighten role and access governance
choices.description: Review the role design, approval boundary, and least-privilege assumptions for the affected workflow.
choices.why: Clarifying authorization boundaries reduces repeat policy exceptions without relying on punitive assumptions about intent.

choices.label: Run targeted role training
choices.description: Reinforce policy intent, escalation options, and approved exception handling for the relevant team.
choices.why: Targeted training can reduce accidental policy deviations and improve shared expectations, though it is not a substitute for access design.

choices.label: Escalate for formal risk review
choices.description: Send the exception to security, risk, and assurance owners for a documented disposition.
choices.why: Formal review improves accountability and evidence while avoiding unsupported conclusions about the cause of the exception.

scenarios.title: Integrity anomaly
scenarios.brief: Monitoring detects an inconsistency between two fictional authoritative record views. The cause is unknown and may be benign, procedural, or technical.
facts: The anomaly is confirmed by two independent observations.
No attribution or hostile cause is assumed.
assumptions: Affected records can be isolated from downstream decision use while review proceeds.
Independent assurance staff are available for corroboration.

choices.label: Contain decision use and validate records
choices.description: Temporarily restrict affected records from downstream use and perform controlled validation against trusted sources.
choices.why: Restricting uncertain records reduces the simulated consequence of bad decisions while independent validation improves confidence.

choices.label: Expand integrity monitoring
choices.description: Broaden comparison coverage and observation cadence to determine the anomaly's scope.
choices.why: Broader monitoring improves scope awareness without asserting a cause and can support a more reliable risk decision.

choices.label: Escalate as an integrity incident
choices.description: Activate the documented incident governance path with security, operations, risk, and assurance stakeholders.
choices.why: Structured escalation improves coordination, ownership, and containment discipline without implying an attack or specific root cause.

scenarios.title: Risk ownership conflict
scenarios.brief: Two fictional teams disagree about who has authority to accept a cross-functional resilience risk before a major planning milestone.
facts: The risk is documented, but the current acceptance authority is ambiguous.
No immediate service disruption is occurring.
assumptions: Executive governance can resolve the authority question within the planning cycle.
The teams can continue limited mitigation while ownership is clarified.

choices.label: Resolve authority through formal escalation
choices.description: Use the risk governance process to assign a single accountable decision owner and document the rationale.
choices.why: Clear authority reduces decision latency and strengthens the evidence trail for acceptance or further mitigation.

choices.label: Refresh risk-owner responsibilities
choices.description: Run a targeted governance session on authority, escalation thresholds, and evidence expectations.
choices.why: Role clarity reduces future ambiguity, though a formal decision is still needed for the current risk.

choices.label: Defer the ownership decision
choices.description: Continue current work and revisit authority after the planning milestone.
choices.why: Deferral preserves near-term capacity but leaves the risk without unambiguous acceptance authority.

scenarios.title: Recovery assurance gap
scenarios.brief: A scheduled resilience review finds that the most recent full-scope recovery exercise is older than the organization intended.
facts: Recovery procedures exist and smaller component tests have passed.
The gap is assurance freshness, not evidence of a current outage.
assumptions: A controlled exercise can be scheduled without disrupting essential services.
The exercise can include dependency and evidence objectives.

choices.label: Run a controlled recovery exercise
choices.description: Exercise priority recovery paths, dependency handoffs, evidence capture, and decision ownership.
choices.why: A controlled exercise tests assumptions, improves recovery confidence, and can reduce both disruption likelihood and consequence in the simulation.

choices.label: Perform recovery assurance review
choices.description: Independently assess procedures, evidence, ownership, and known gaps before the next exercise.
choices.why: Assurance improves the quality of the recovery assessment and highlights gaps, but does not substitute for exercising the process.

choices.label: Escalate the overdue assurance gap
choices.description: Assign executive visibility and a time-bounded commitment for the full-scope exercise.
choices.why: Escalation improves accountability and reduces the chance that the assurance gap remains indefinitely unresolved.
